before.title: 2.0 dCi diesel particulate filter (DPF) blockage
before.description: The 2.0 dCi diesel Koleos (130/150/175 hp variants) is prone to DPF clogging, especially when driven mainly on short, low-speed trips that never allow the filter to reach regeneration temperature. Symptoms include reduced power / limp mode, visible smoke, and a DPF warning light. Faulty differential pressure or exhaust temperature sensors can worsen or falsely trigger the problem, and a botched dealer forced-regeneration has in some cases destroyed the filter outright.
before.solution: Take the vehicle on periodic longer motorway drives at moderate-to-high RPM to allow passive/active regeneration; verify the differential-pressure and exhaust-temp sensors are working. A clogged filter can often be professionally cleaned (~€100); a destroyed DPF requires replacement (£1,300-£2,000+).

proposal.title: 2.0 dCi diesel particulate filter (DPF) blockage
proposal.description: The frozen page applies one DPF-blockage identity to 2.0 dCi variants across first- and second-generation Koleos vehicles from 2008-2020, omitting 2016 while combining soot loading, pressure/temperature sensors, short-trip use, smoke and an alleged filter-destroying dealer regeneration. Forum, advice and app-community pages do not establish one manufacturer-defined population, cause, mileage or repair price.
proposal.solution: Capture DTCs, soot and ash estimates, differential pressure, exhaust temperatures and regeneration history, then test pressure pipes/sensors, EGR, intake/boost, fueling and oil dilution before cleaning or forced regeneration. Do not force regeneration until filter load, oil level, sensor validity and exhaust-temperature safety are confirmed. Do not buy a DPF, sensor or pipe from this page; emissions generation, root cause and VIN fitment must be established first.

before.title: 2.5 petrol (QR25DE/2TR) timing chain stretch and oil consumption
before.description: The first-generation 2.5-litre petrol Koleos uses the Renault 2TR engine, essentially the Nissan QR25DE. After roughly 100,000-150,000 km many owners experience excessive oil consumption (worn piston rings) and timing chain stretch, often signalled by a rattle on cold start. Delayed oil changes or incorrect oil viscosity accelerate wear of the chain tensioner and guides.
before.solution: Maintain strict oil-change intervals with the correct viscosity and monitor oil level between changes. Investigate any cold-start rattle promptly; a stretched chain requires replacement of the chain, tensioner and guides, and heavy oil burning may need a ring/top-end rebuild.

proposal.solution: Confirm the exact engine code, document oil consumption against distance and inspect leaks, crankcase ventilation, compression/leak-down, plugs and exhaust condition. For cold-start noise, verify oil pressure, localize the source and check cam/crank timing under engine-specific Renault procedures before disturbing the drive. Do not buy piston rings, a chain kit, tensioner or guides from this page; failed path, engine identity and VIN fitment must be established first.

before.title: AWD rear differential / transfer case internal failure (2.0 dCi 4x4)
before.description: On 2.0 dCi all-wheel-drive Koleos models, the rear differential can fail internally and even crack through its housing, typically between 80,000-100,000 km (sometimes earlier). Owners report oil leaks from the halfshafts and find 1-5mm metal chunks in the differential oil, indicating gear destruction. The failure can recur even after repair if the underlying cause (low oil level / overheating, coupling stress) is not addressed.
before.solution: Check rear differential and transfer-case oil level and condition regularly from around 60,000 km, and change the diff fluid on a strict interval. Inspect for metal contamination early; once gears are damaged the differential (and sometimes the coupling/transfer unit) must be rebuilt or replaced.
symptoms: Whining or grinding from rear of vehicle
Oil leak from halfshafts / diff housing
Vibration or clunk under AWD load

proposal.solution: Identify the exact AWD architecture and complaint location, inspect leaks, tire-size equality and driveline binding, then sample the specified unit fluids and measure backlash, bearing noise and metal contamination before disassembly. Stop if severe noise, binding, leakage or loss of drive is present. Do not buy a differential, coupling, transfer unit or fluid from this page; failed unit, damage extent, lubricant specification and VIN fitment must be established first.

before.solution: Perform a complete CVT fluid exchange with genuine Renault NS-2 or NS-3 fluid. Replace the CVT belt and pulleys if slip is confirmed. Update CVT control module software.

before.title: Front lower suspension arm fracture (2011 recall)
before.description: On Koleos vehicles produced January-November 2011, the right-hand forward lower suspension arm can break, particularly when braking force is applied. If the arm breaks the car can suddenly veer to the right and the wheel can become jammed inside the wheel arch, creating a serious crash risk. Renault issued an official recall in 2013 to replace the affected arm.
before.solution: Have the recall remedy performed at a Renault dealer (free of charge) — the faulty lower suspension arm is replaced. Owners of 2011 units should verify via VIN that the recall has been completed.
symptoms: Car veers to one side under braking
Clunking or knocking from front suspension
Wheel jammed in arch / loss of control

before.title: X-Tronic CVT transmission failure (slipping, shuddering, high revs)
before.description: The Jatco-sourced X-Tronic CVT used in the Koleos is the single most reported failure point. Owners report gear slipping, shuddering on shifts, hesitation under acceleration, and the engine flaring to high RPM in Drive (belt slip / loss of hydraulic pressure), typically after around 100,000 km. A known contributing cause is the transmission oil cooler allowing engine coolant to mix into the transmission fluid, contaminating and destroying internal components. Complete transmission replacement is common and expensive.
before.solution: Replace CVT fluid every ~60,000-80,000 km (sooner for heavy city/stop-start use) with the correct Renault/Jatco NS-3 spec fluid, and inspect for coolant cross-contamination at the cooler. Early intervention (fluid + cooler) can prevent failure; once the belt/valve body is damaged, a transmission rebuild or replacement is required.
symptoms: High RPM / engine flaring in Drive
Grinding or whining noise from transmission
